claims.text: Cast refractory multi-principal-element alloys can exhibit limited ductility because they contain coarse brittle silicide, B2, or Laves secondary phases.
HfMoTaTiZr can have a single-phase BCC constitution.
A severe-plastic-deformation and low-temperature-aging route can simultaneously produce grains below 50 nm and coherent precipitates in the proposed refractory alloy.
Multistage thermomechanical processing of a W-based alloy can generate independently controllable coherent Ni3Ta-based delta and gamma-double-prime precipitates.
The coherent delta and gamma-double-prime precipitates have D0a and D022 structures, respectively.
Aging below the coherent-precipitate solvus but above the rapid-grain-growth temperature provides a processing window that retains grains below 50 nm.
Restricting aging time prevents coherent nanoprecipitates from coarsening or transforming into brittle TCP phases.
Coherent nanoprecipitates pin grain boundaries and thereby stabilize a nanocrystalline grain size.
Coherent nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion and provide precipitation hardening.
Rapid cooling followed by controlled aging kinetically suppresses equilibrium Laves and silicide formation while favoring coherent metastable precipitates.
Nanocrystalline grain refinement increases strength through Hall-Petch grain-boundary strengthening.
Coherent precipitate interfaces prevent the crack initiation associated with brittle intermetallic interfaces and consequently improve ductility.
The proposed route will produce grains smaller than 50 nm.
The resulting material will contain a BCC solid-solution matrix with coherent D0a and D022 nanoprecipitates.
The resulting material will have yield strength above 2000 MPa and uniform tensile ductility above 10%.
The proposed microstructure will avoid brittle fracture associated with coarse Laves or silicide phases.
Conventional cast refractory HEAs typically have less than 5% ductility.
Exceeding the coherent-precipitate solvus causes coarsening or transformation into Laves, sigma, or mu TCP phases.
Failure to refine the grains below 50 nm causes a loss of Hall-Petch strengthening.

contradictions.description: The structure is called dual-phase, but a BCC matrix plus two crystallographically distinct precipitates, D0a delta and D022 gamma-double-prime, constitutes at least three phases unless one precipitate type is absent or both are being grouped nonstandardly.

The stated processing window is above the temperature for rapid grain growth, while the mediator and outcome require preservation of a sub-50-nm grain structure; no balancing kinetic condition is specified.

The prediction requires yield strength above 2000 MPa and ductility above 10%, whereas the falsification thresholds are only below 1500 MPa or below 5%. Results between these thresholds could miss the prediction without clearly falsifying it.
